A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CLEWS research work. The complete main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison; v3's extra page comes from bibliography reflow.

before.justification: v2 reports original CLEWS experiments on DiscogsVI-YT and SHS100k-v2, including track and segment retrieval, ablations, and runtime measurements (Section 5; Appendix C).

after.justification: v3 retains the original CLEWS benchmark experiments, ablations, and runtime measurements in Section 5 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain identical segment-distance reductions, contrastive loss, network architecture, and training and inference procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use DiscogsVI-YT and SHS100k-v2 for track and segment retrieval. The evaluated data, tasks, and query scenarios, including the Appendix C evaluations, are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in corresponding benchmark and loss comparisons. This includes the ByteCover variants in Table 2 and Re-MOVE among the reported random-segment MAP comparisons in Table 7.

E3.justification: Dataset partitions, preprocessing, training budgets, query lengths, hop sizes, distance-reduction rules, and MAP/NAR metrics are unchanged. Both versions retain the same best-match and random-segment evaluation protocols.

E4.justification: Both contain the same reduction and loss ablations (Tables 3–4), hyperparameter sensitivity analysis (Figure 3), alternative segment-protocol evaluation, and runtime analysis (Appendix C). No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: The same 95% confidence intervals and shaded uncertainty bands appear in both versions. Run/seed information and statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All reported result entries and empirical plots match, including Appendix C. For example, Table 2 retains CLEWS's DVI-Test NAR of 2.70 ± 0.05 and SHS-Test MAP of 0.876 ± 0.005.

T1.justification: The reduction definitions, loss and gradient derivations, numerical reformulation in Appendix A.2, corrected NAR definition in Appendix B.2, and complexity expressions in Appendix C.3 are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about learning from weakly labeled segments, the proposed contrastive loss, retrieval performance, and potential applicability beyond musical version matching.

C2.justification: Interpretations of partial matching and loss behavior, difficulty with very short queries, numerical stability caveats, and criticism of random-segment evaluation remain unchanged (Section 5; Appendices A.2 and C.2).

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, software versions, hardware, training times, and preprocessing instructions are identical. The code/checkpoint access statements and PDF link targets are also unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, novelty positioning, and complete reference list are unchanged. The added personal acknowledgement introduces no cited work or revised relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v3 adds a sentence thanking Toshimitsu Uesaka for comments on an earlier version and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The remaining prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The longer acknowledgement reflows the bibliography, leaving its final reference alone on page 11 and shifting the appendices by one page. Figures 1–6 and Tables 1–8 retain their content, formatting, and captions.

improvement.justification: v3 adds an acknowledgement while preserving all scientific explanations, experiments, results, and reproducibility information, including Appendices A–C. The resulting bibliography reflow adds a mostly empty page but does not meaningfully change clarity, evidential support, or overall paper quality.
